item.title: What Makes Software Good Has Changed
item.description: The definition of good software has split into two realities. Most leaders still haven’t realized it.

item.title: When Infrastructure Fails: The Leadership Accountability Gap
item.description: From AWS outages to Germany’s Telematikinfrastruktur, 2025 showed that resilience isn’t built in data centers — it’s enforced by leadership that understands complexity and owns interdependencies.

item.title: The micro-apps revolution: Can building software be too easy?
item.description: AI-created micro-apps are creating technical debt faster than ever, while eroding the very skills that make engineering teams valuable. How do CTOs shift from managing execution to managing decision quality at scale?

item.title: The Enforcement Trap: Why Pressuring Developers Guarantees Failure
item.description: It’s 2025, 12 years after “The Phoenix Project”. Yet, there are companies that seem to be unaware of product and development culture.

item.title: Leaders vs. Managers: Decoding the Dance in the Tech Arena
item.description: On the fundamental difference between a leader and a manger, and why it is a good thing to have both.

item.title: Dethroning the Idol: A Multi-Disciplinary Look at Leadership and Beyond
item.description: Looking at different leader types from military, business and tech - and why they’re called leaders.

item.title: Taking a Step Back to Leap Forward: A Reflection on Career Choices
item.description: Three years later, data confirms that stepping back from leadership wasn’t retreat — it was strategic repositioning.

item.title: The Crew Manifest – Building the Team That Builds the Company
item.description: Vision gives direction, mindset defines motion. The team turns both into reality. Building the right crew is the CTO’s most important design decision.

item.title: The Cultural Compass – Vision and Mindset as the CTO's True Leverage
item.description: A CTO’s true influence begins long before code is written. It lies in shaping a clear vision and the company mindset that turns that vision into motion.

item.title: The CTO trap
item.description: Walking the thin line between being an executive, tech lead and human being in a company.
